findings.title: Primary GitHub CTA links to non-existent repo (HTTP 404)
findings.description: Footer conversion CTA 'GitHub â†—' targets https://github.com/buff-lang/buff, which returns HTTP 404 (mechanically verified via live fetch). Same broken target at website/benchmarks.html:514 and playground/index.html:54 ('docs â†—'). Canonical origin is https://github.com/vinaosb/buff.git (git remote -v); README badges correctly use vinaosb/buff. The main conversion link on every marketing page dead-ends.
findings.root_cause: Pages were authored against an anticipated 'buff-lang' GitHub org that was never created; the repo actually lives under the personal 'vinaosb' account.
findings.impact: All acquisition clicks from the website footer, benchmarks footer, and playground docs button 404 â€” direct conversion loss and a broken first impression at launch.
findings.recommendation: Point all three links at the canonical repo, or create/transfer to the buff-lang org. Then sweep the repo for remaining buff-lang/buff references (installers, README install taps) before launch.

fix_examples.before: GitHub â†—
fix_examples.after: GitHub â†—

findings.fix_guide: 1) Confirm canonical with git remote -v. 2) Replace github.com/buff-lang/buff with github.com/vinaosb/buff in website/index.html:402, website/benchmarks.html:514, playground/index.html:54. 3) grep -r 'buff-lang/buff' across installers/docs for stragglers. 4) Re-run website + playground Playwright suites.

effort_estimate.breakdown: 5 min decide canonical target + 5 min edit 3 files + 5 min repo-wide sweep/test

detection_method.query: href github.com/buff-lang/buff vs origin remote vinaosb/buff; live GET returned 404

findings.verification_command: Select-String -Path website\*.html,playground\index.html -Pattern 'buff-lang/buff'; try { Invoke-WebRequest 'https://github.com/buff-lang/buff' -UseBasicParsing | Select-Object StatusCode } catch { $_.Exception.Response.StatusCode.value__ }; git remote -v

confidence.rationale: 404 confirmed via live HTTP fetch; canonical remote confirmed via git; all three occurrences enumerated and read.

fp_risk_self_assessment.reasoning: Mechanically verified 404 plus remote mismatch; not a style opinion. Residual risk: org could be created later, retroactively validating links.
fp_risk_self_assessment.verified_against_conventions: root AGENTS.md (no convention mandates a buff-lang org), README.md badge URLs

findings.title: Playground CTA path inconsistent; breaks in deployed Pages layout
findings.description: benchmarks.html nav 'Playground' CTA uses ../playground/index.html while website/index.html and website/app.js try-links use ./playground/index.html. pages.yml publishes website/* at the site root with playground/ as a subdirectory, so the DEPLOYED benchmarks page escapes the site root and 404s; conversely index.html CTAs 404 when website/ is served raw locally. Exactly one path form can be correct per serving layout.
findings.root_cause: benchmarks.html was authored assuming repo-root-relative serving, while the Pages publish layout (and index.html/app.js) assume website/ as the site root.
findings.impact: Benchmark-page visitors (high-intent traffic) lose the playground conversion path in production; local raw-serving breaks the hero CTAs instead.
findings.recommendation: Standardize on ./playground/index.html to match the pages.yml deployed layout; fix benchmarks.html:196. Document in website/README.md that local preview must serve the publish-layout root, not website/ alone.
findings.fix_guide: 1) Confirm publish layout in .github/workflows/pages.yml (website/* to root; playground to ./playground/). 2) Edit benchmarks.html:196 to ./playground/index.html. 3) Smoke-test the deployed <pages-url>/benchmarks.html Playground button. 4) Optionally extend website.spec.cjs with a link-target-exists assertion.

effort_estimate.breakdown: 2 min edit + 8 min verify against pages.yml layout and tests

detection_method.query: '(\./|\.\./)playground/index\.html' hrefs across website/*.html + website/app.js vs pages.yml publish-directory assembly

confidence.rationale: Path resolution and publish layout are mechanically verified; residual uncertainty is only which serving layout the maintainer considers canonical.

fp_risk_self_assessment.reasoning: Breakage depends on deployment root; pages.yml (deployed) verified as the layout, but a maintainer intending repo-root serving would flip the fix direction.
fp_risk_self_assessment.verified_against_conventions: website/README.md deploy section, playground/README.md deploy section, root AGENTS.md

findings.title: Registry download metrics exist â€” aggregate-only, privacy-clean
findings.description: The only usage-metrics surface in the repo: every tarball download calls record_download (handlers.rs:861); per-package totals are exposed via GET /api/v1/packages/{name}/stats ({"downloads":N}) and feed search ranking. Storage rows are keyed (name, version, count) only â€” storage_sqlite.rs:703, storage.rs:401 defaults to 0. No user/IP attribution is persisted; the IP rate-limiter keeps rolling 5-minute in-memory timestamps, pruned per request, never exposed. No action required â€” documented for the audit trail.
findings.root_cause: T57 stats feature shipped by design; registry AGENTS.md lists download stats as an intended capability, not an accident.
findings.impact: None â€” aggregate counts are standard registry practice (crates.io parity); no personal data collected or retained.
findings.recommendation: Optional doc-only: add a retention/privacy note stating download counts are aggregate and IP rate-limit state is in-memory with 5-minute TTL, before any public deployment.

fix_examples.before: /// Returns the total download count for `name` across all versions.
fix_examples.after:
/// Returns the total download count for `name` across all versions.
/// Aggregate-only: no caller IP or user identity is recorded with a download.

findings.fix_guide: 1) Append aggregate-only wording to get_stats docs and lib.rs route docs. 2) No code change required. 3) Revisit only if a real backend adds request logging.

effort_estimate.breakdown: 15 min doc comments; no code/tests touched

detection_method.query: download_count|record_download|metrics across crates/buff-registry/src; route arm packages/{name}/stats in lib.rs:284

confidence.rationale: Both storage backends, the stats handler, and the rate limiter were read in full; no user-keyed metrics anywhere in the crate.

fp_risk_self_assessment.reasoning: Reported as clean/informational, not a violation; every backend verified aggregate-only and the IP limiter verified volatile/in-memory.
fp_risk_self_assessment.verified_against_conventions: crates/buff-registry/AGENTS.md (in-memory MVP, DEFERRED list), root AGENTS.md pure-Rust rules

findings.title: Third-party font/CDN fetches are the only external requests â€” zero beacons
findings.description: Exhaustive read of website/ and playground/ HTML+JS found ZERO analytics (no GA/GTM/Plausible/segment/mixpanel/posthog/sendBeacon). Only third-party fetches: Google Fonts CSS (website/index.html:11-13, benchmarks.html:10-12, playground/index.html:12-14) and CodeMirror 5 from cdnjs (playground/index.html:17-23). Google Fonts logs visitor IPs (GDPR enforcement precedent); cdnjs is a supply-chain surface. Playground wasm loads from local ./pkg only â€” no phoning home.
findings.root_cause: Convenience CDN links chosen at site creation; privacy-hardening (self-hosting) was never prioritized pre-launch.
findings.impact: Minor: visitor IPs disclosed to Google on every page load; pages degrade offline; a CDN outage breaks playground editor. Not a tracking violation â€” flagged for completeness only.
findings.recommendation: Self-host the three font families as woff2 (fontsource or google-webfonts-helper) and vendor CodeMirror 5.65.16 into playground/vendor/ for a zero-third-party, offline-capable static site.
findings.fix_guide: 1) Download woff2 for IBM Plex Mono/Sans + Space Mono into website/fonts/ and playground/fonts/. 2) Write local @font-face CSS. 3) Vendor codemirror.min.js/css + rust mode + 3 addons into playground/vendor/, update 6 tags in index.html. 4) Verify offline (serve, block network, transpile still works) and re-run both Playwright suites.

effort_estimate.breakdown: 45 min fonts + 30 min CodeMirror vendoring + 30 min offline verification + 15 min Playwright re-run

detection_method.query: googletagmanager|gtag\(|plausible|segment|mixpanel|amplitude|posthog|umami|matomo|hotjar|sendBeacon|beacon|telemetry|analytics over website/** + playground/** (0 matches); https?:// sweep (fonts + cdnjs only)

confidence.rationale: Every HTML/JS line of both static sites was read plus keyword greps; residual risk limited to runtime CDN content, not repo code.

fp_risk_self_assessment.reasoning: Fonts are NOT analytics â€” main risk is over-reporting; mitigated by the explicit zero-beacon verdict and completeness-only framing.
fp_risk_self_assessment.verified_against_conventions: root AGENTS.md (website/playground documented as static, no build step), website/README.md, playground/README.md
